title: We just launched the ML backtesting infrastructure for trademates. Results are mixed and that's the point.
author: tradematesHQ
selftext:
In the last two months we developed our backtesting ML system for tradmates.co. Obvious next question from users: does it actually work?

So we started saving every score with the price at analysis time, then check the 90d return vs SPY. Alpha, not raw return. If SPY rips 8% and our "buy" does 7%, that's a miss.

Also grading the fair-value range: did price land inside, above, or below what the model predicted.

Anything with >10% alpha miss gets flagged and re-analyzed to see what the model got wrong. Thesis drift, missed catalyst, sector rotation, whatever. Logged, not swept under the rug. For each stock we create a knowledge base where we write down why the analysis was wrong if the stock price has a delta >10% to our prediction.

Currently sitting at \~+3% median alpha across tracked names. Small sample yet but will look different in 6 months. Our users analyse up to 400 different stocks per week and >1000 per month. Each stock is being backtested. Each analysis creates its own pricing history. The ML system adjusts the weighting model over time and with each analysis it gets more refined.

Our point isn't to say "look how good our AI Investment score is." Point is if you ship a scoring system and don't measure it against reality you're just vibes.

https://preview.redd.it/flee2xi367fh1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=e42b87bcd8070419acf8fc752ebe0d81ba94f2fe

Screenshot of the hypothetical equal-weight track record widget above. Per-ticker backtest panel goes live once the first batch hits the 90d mark.

Happy to nerd out on the methodology (FX handling, benchmark choice, why 90d and not 30/180) if useful.
